paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: Jesus knows exactly what is coming, and He stays at the table anyway. He says, "one of you will betray Me," and He still gives the morsel to Judas (John 13:21, 26). Then He turns to the eleven who are left, troubled and confused, and gives them something to hold. You don't have to have the night figured out for Jesus to be steady in it.

The new commandment is the heart of it: "Love one another. As I have loved you, so you also must love one another." (John 13:34) Notice the measuring stick. It's not how nice you feel today, it's the way Jesus has loved them. And He says "By this everyone will know that you are My disciples, if you love one another." (John 13:35) I've stamped a lot of cookies, and nobody ever knew whose kitchen they came from by the shape alone. They knew by the love that came with them.

Then there's Peter, and I think he's the one most of us see ourselves in. He says, "I will lay down my life for You," and I believe he means every word of it (John 13:37). Jesus still tells him, "before the rooster crows, you will deny Me three times." (John 13:38) So bring your big promises to Jesus, friend, but lean on His love for you more than on your love for Him. His love is the one that doesn't wobble.
